_comment: THE DIG AND THE KILL ARE SEQUENTIAL PHASES, SO THEIR ITERATION COUNTS ADD --
MTG_EDF_GOFF_PHASES.
Reconstructed from an autonomous turn-5 board (COMBO OFF sweep state X-2d1c5c7375, engine game
29 of the sweep's own 57-game corpus).  Emiel the Blessed + Peregrine Drake, net +7 a pass,
net_c +3, Living Wish still in the LIBRARY: rule WISH-DRAW.
FlickerGoOffCount used to size such a loop as
max(iterations by MANA, dig_draws, iterations by {C} PIPS)
which is right for three demands on ONE resource and wrong for two phases that cannot overlap.
A finisher fetched out of the library is not on the battlefield until the dig has found the
Living Wish, so not one of its {C} pips can be spent during the dig -- the iterations that supply
those pips are the ones AFTER the deploy.  The max therefore sizes the loop to whichever phase is
longer instead of to both, and the apply spends the whole count digging and then has nothing left
to drain with.  (Raising MTG_EDF_MAX_ITER does NOT help, and that is the tell: the count is not
being clamped, it is being computed wrong.)
A/B on this fixture (one binary) -- note the COUNT, which is the lever's own signature:
default                  -> blink Peregrine Drake x35, COMBO OFF verified, opponent dead
MTG_EDF_GOFF_PHASES=0    -> blink Peregrine Drake x22, offered but NOT verified, no win
The same lever on the user's own replayed `claude_s1_gi0` turn 3 (replay-hunt ids RR-9261bc55b5,
RR-1402c9760d, RR-53d4d2273c and their siblings, ordinals 6..8 of that turn): the click goes from
winning on turn 6 to winning on turn 3, the turn it is offered on.
